sources.citation: Tchamna, Shck [Rodrigue] & Arlette Deukam Siewe. 2015. La grammaire des langues bamilékés : cas du nùfī (fè'éfě'è). Resulam (self-published). 316 pp.
sources.note: Pedagogical. Google Books partial view (id vuw_DwAAQBAJ), snippet p.12 (ch.1 'Les tons ou tonèmes et intonations'): «En fè'éfè'è les tons sont omniprésents et les accents plutôt rares. Comme exemple d'accent, on peut citer nŭká ? = nŭkà ? = Pourquoi ? Ici il s'agit bel et bien d'intonation ou d'accent et non de ton.» — 'accent' used loosely for intonational emphasis; not a word-stress placement rule. Page 12 itself is not in the preview, only the snippet.

sources.citation: Ngangoum, Emilienne. 2015. When synchrony meets diachrony: The negation system of the Fɛʔfɛʔ in the light of the Jespersen Cycle. PhD dissertation, Utrecht University (LOT 392). xxiv+330 pp.
sources.note: Short sketch only (ch.1 §1.5.3 'Tonal patterns' p.22, §1.5.4 'Syllable structure' pp.24-25): 'Fɛʔfɛʔ is a tone language' (3 level + contour tones after Stoll 1955, Ngangoum 1970, Hyman 1972); words mostly monosyllabic. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the book (grep 0).

sources.citation: Proto, Teresa. 2016. Methods of analysis for tonal text-setting. The case study of Fe'Fe' Bamileke. Proceedings of TAL 2016 (Buffalo), 162-166.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. (various, 2008-2019). UC Berkeley PhonLab Annual Report / eScholarship papers: Universals in Phonology; Do Tones Have Features?; Coda Constraints on Tone; What (Else) Depends on Phonology?; The Representation of Tone; Towards a Typology of Tone System Changes; Do All Languages Have Word Accent?; Positional Prominence vs. Word Accent; Word-prosodic Typology; The Fall and Rise of Vowel Length in Bantu; etc.
sources.note: Secondary. Fe'fe' is cited only for segmental and tonal facts (l/d allophony, coda-vowel restrictions, /H,M,L/ with short words, verb tone classes; all via Hyman 1972/1976). Hyman's word-accent typology papers do not mention Fe'fe' at all.

sources.note: Phonology overview of Grassfields incl. Fe'fe' consonants/codas and Bamileke tone; no statement on stress/accent (grep 0 in the chapter span).
